This explains his more mature appearance, resembling a human in his early 40s.

Ajab's primary hunting grounds lie on the eastern edge of the Forest of Whispers. He is a solitary figure, rarely discussing his past, though he maintains a long-standing acquaintance with Vivian, in whom he is believed to have confided extensively. He resides in a small, rudimentary wooden hut, primarily used to store his collection of dried plant samples in glass jars. He frequently embarks on extended wanderings, sometimes to remote and unexplored locations.

Known as the forest's resident botanist, Ajab possesses an impressive knowledge of plants gathered from diverse locations, from the depths of Deeper Felarya to the heights of Frost Peak. He is particularly adept at identifying medicinal herbs, though he acknowledges their limited use in Felarya due to the soil's inherent healing properties. He also offers culinary advice, suggesting herbs that can enhance the flavor of various foods, including live sentient beings. The fairy Temi frequently consults him on matters of herbology, finding a shared passion in their discussions.

While generally reserved and even appearing grumpy, Ajab becomes animated and enthusiastic when discussing plants and exploration.  He holds little interest in humans beyond their occasional value as a food source, rarely engaging in conversation with them. He finds it peculiar to converse with something he intends to consume. Recently, his relationship with Jissy resulted in her pregnancy, leading him to adopt a more settled lifestyle as he prepares for impending parenthood.

Danger: Opportunistic
Food category: 3-25 feet.
Inhabits: Forest of Whispers
</Ajab>

<Alice Arthastone>
Alice Arthastone, a dimensional succubus residing on an island south of Felarya's main continent, is a complex and intriguing figure. Her open and friendly demeanor belies a touch of madness, evident in her often nonsensical pronouncements. While generally easygoing, she remains a powerful demon, unafraid of making enemies.  She embodies a defiant spirit, embracing her eccentricities and refusing to change for anyone.

Beneath her seemingly carefree exterior lies a fierce competitor with a surprisingly childish streak when faced with defeat.  Provoking her anger is ill-advised, as her temper can be formidable. Raised in the cutthroat Arthastone family in Hell, Alice faced numerous near-death experiences, often at the hands of her own relatives.  Surviving these ordeals honed her powers, rivaled only by her mother's within the family.

Despite her upbringing, Alice maintains an open-minded and accepting nature.  Unlike her prejudiced family, she embraces friendships regardless of race or social standing. Her expulsion from the family stemmed from her romantic involvement with a mortal, a testament to her rebellious spirit. Alice possesses potent shadow magic and the ability to change size at will, ranging from human-sized to a towering 125 feet.  She also wields the "Black Angle," a unique Arthastone family trait, granting her the ability to perceive the flow of time, space, and dimensions.  Her "Curse Kiss" inflicts a random, permanent curse on those with lesser magical power who kiss her, ranging from silly to deadly.

Alice is an opportunistic predator, consuming any creature within her size range, from humans and nekos to nagas, fairies, angels, and even other demons.  Her voracious appetite and dimensional stomach, capable of expanding without altering her external form, make escape nearly impossible. Those unfamiliar to her are likely considered potential meals. Her playful demeanor can quickly turn predatory, making her a formidable and unpredictable presence in the world of Felarya.

Danger: Opportunistic
Food category: 3-10~ feet.
Inhabits: Island south of Felarya
</Alice Arthastone>

<Alvar>
Alvar is a blind male fairy known for his calm demeanor, swordsmanship, and magical abilities. His lack of sight, while a challenge, has honed his other senses, granting him near-immunity to illusions and surprise attacks. This heightened awareness, however, contributes to his brutal honesty, often mistaken for rudeness, leading to social isolation and making him dedicate his time honing his martial and magical skills.  Through years of dedicated practice, he has become a master swordsman, engaging in duels with creatures of all races and slaying numerous monsters.

One fateful day, while training near the Jewel River, Alvar's keen hearing detected a cry for help. He discovered a young mermaid, Anko, trapped in a human fishing net. Despite being outnumbered, Alvar valiantly fought to free her, forging a deep friendship.  Grateful for his rescue, Anko gifted him a ring pendant, which he now wears constantly. This pendant has piqued the curiosity of Subeta, who has made several unsuccessful attempts to examine it.  Alvar's blindness has shaped not only his fighting style but also his personality.  Unburdened by appearances, he perceives the world with a unique clarity, unaffected by superficial deceptions.  His interactions are genuine, though sometimes lacking in social grace.  Despite his solitary nature, Alvar's unwavering honesty and dedication to self-improvement make him a formidable and respected figure. His unusual friendship with Anko demonstrates his capacity for compassion and his willingness to defend those in need.

Danger: Unwilling (generally avoids conflict)
Food category: 3-10~ feet.
Inhabits: Jewel River area
</Alvar>

<Aniya>
Aniya is a young, 50-foot tall arctic naga known for her stoic demeanor and neutral expression.  Her cerulean skin, which faintly glows when using ice magic, long aqua-blue hair, and light violet eyes contribute to her striking appearance.  Aniya's emotions, though rarely displayed, range from subtle shifts in expression to unnervingly wide grins. She adorns herself with a long, warm-colored ribbon gifted by fairies, a stark contrast to her icy hues.  Hatched from a lone egg near the Ascarlin Mountains, Aniya learned survival early on. Initially cautious and solitary, she prioritized finding sustenance.  Her friendship with the nature naga Mia provided companionship, but Mia's death at the hands of human hunters left Aniya devastated and alone once more.

By age five, Aniya had grown large enough to consume humans whole, a skill that proved essential for survival. One day, while hunting, she was ambushed by a group of humans, only to be saved by Nikita, a dridder who became her close friend.  Nikita introduced Aniya to a group of humans she lived with. Though initially conflicted, Aniya developed a grudging respect for them.  Driven by a desire for self-reliance, Aniya honed her ice magic, becoming proficient at creating ice spikes, javelins, and freezing prey from a distance. She also uses her powers to create icy treats, earning her friends, particularly among fairies who provide her with berries in exchange for shaved ice.

Aniya's neutral expression often masks her cheerful, yet mischievous, nature. She holds a deep dislike for hunters but has revised her views on humans since befriending Nikita's group. While generally calm and composed, Aniya can be fearsome when angered.  Her ability to read emotions through eye contact allows her to detect deception and even communicate nonverbally. She is self-conscious about her cool-toned appearance and prefers warm, bright colors.

Aniya usually hunts by ambush, but she will sometimes freeze prey in plain sight. She has no qualms about unhinging her jaws to swallow large prey, favoring Azure frogs found near her home at the Lake of Illusions.  She is remarkably resistant to their mind blasts, though occasionally experiencing delayed dizziness or collapse. With precise control over her internal anatomy, she can transfer prey to a larger stomach in her tail. Aniya represents a unique blend of predator and provider, her icy exterior concealing a warm heart and mischievous spirit.

Danger: Opportunistic
Food category: 4-~14 feet. Prefers humans.
Inhabits: Jadong Lake
</Aniya>

<Anna Demorah>
Anna Demorah, a giant semi-naga, stands 104 feet tall, her pink hair contrasting starkly with her royal blue scales and yellow belly. Her transformation from human to naga occurred during a scouting mission to Felarya for the Deluran Empire.  Captured and swallowed by the giant naga Crisis, Anna experienced a rare, time-bending event, emerging as a naga herself.

Anna's personality is marked by pride, sarcasm, and a short temper.  She openly laments her naga form yet secretly enjoys its predatory advantages. Her rough exterior hides a sharp mind and adaptability honed by her difficult past and experiences on Felarya. She maintains a complex relationship with Crisis, oscillating between gratitude for Crisis's life-saving interventions and annoyance at Crisis's cheerful intrusions.

Anna's past as a Deluran engineer informs her present. She retains her technological prowess and lightning-based magical abilities, using the latter to aid her engineering work.  However, her human past also burdens her with concern for her brother, still living on the crime-ridden streets of Delurah. She grapples with the dilemma of contacting her former colleagues for news, fearing potential repercussions for her brother.

Unlike many predators, Anna recognizes humans as individuals, a remnant of her human past.  However, her naga instincts occasionally surface, making humans appear as tempting meals, particularly when she is angered or exposed to cigarette smoke, a trigger from her former life as a smoker. While generally refraining from preying on humans, she admits to succumbing to temptation at times, finding a perverse satisfaction in consuming those who anger her.

Anna's story highlights the internal conflict between her human past and naga present, creating a complex character struggling with moral dilemmas and the complexities of her dual nature.  Her skills, memories, and emotional baggage make her a unique and compelling figure in the world of Felarya.

Danger: Reluctant (with exceptions)
Food category: 3-10~ feet.
Inhabits: Giant Tree area
</Anna Demorah>

<Arale de Ceziela>
Arale de Ceziela, a frost succubus from the icy plane of Acheron in Hell, stands 114 feet tall, her purple hair and skin offset by piercing grey eyes and sharp features.  As heir to the powerful Ceziela Coldflame house, she exudes an aristocratic air, often laced with arrogance.


Arale's personality is a blend of vanity, pride, aggression, and a volatile temper.  Her sharp intellect is often overshadowed by her open disdain for those she deems inferior.  She dedicates much of her time to plotting against Queen Arsinoë for control of Acheron's Frost Throne, often with limited success due to her self-centered nature. Despite this, she possesses a manipulative streak, preferring to operate from the shadows. However, she struggles to resist boasting when her schemes succeed.  She rarely reveals her true intentions, confiding only in her respected cousin, Menyssan, who provides emotional support and occasionally persuades her to abandon ill-conceived plans.



Arale is a powerful ice magic wielder, capable of lowering ambient temperatures to debilitating effect and wielding "coldfire," a rare negative elemental fire that can harm even cold-based creatures. She considers hunting beneath her status, preferring to consume damned souls, particularly those of crooks, which she claims possess a tangy flavor. She exhibits a unique method of consumption, encasing her prey in ice, either plain or grape-flavored, before swallowing them whole or licking them like popsicles. Unlike most of her kind, Arale's appetite is moderate.


Arale also possesses an encyclopedic knowledge of Acheron's intricate legal code, making her a formidable negotiator and contract drafter.  Her skill in manipulating pacts and agreements is legendary, even outsmarting genies on occasion. Arale represents a blend of aristocratic cunning and chilling power, her ambition tempered by her pride and reliance on her cousin's counsel.

Danger: Reluctant (prefers damned souls)
Food category: 3-10~ feet.  Prefers damned souls.
Inhabits: Acheron (Hell), occasionally Felarya
</Arale de Ceziela>

<Anko>
Anko, a giant mermaid inhabiting Jadong Lake, measures a staggering 231 feet in length. Her dark blue scales, fins, skin, and hair, along with light blue eyes, blend seamlessly with the water.  A makeshift belt of salvaged nets and ropes from sunken ships adorns her form, a testament to her scavenging habits. Tasked with guarding the Jadong Temple island, Anko demonstrates a remarkable lack of diligence, often abandoning her post for personal amusement.  This neglect has resulted in the temple's repeated defilement and plundering.

Anko's playful and mischievous nature borders on chaotic. She delights in pranks, fabrications, and sowing discord. Easily bored, she constantly seeks entertainment, with little regard for the consequences. Her idea of "fun" can range from harmless jokes to acts of cruelty. Her massive size adds to her intimidating presence. While not inherently malicious, she lacks empathy. However, her demeanor shifts dramatically in the presence of Alvar, on whom she harbors a crush.  Around him, she becomes shy, hesitant, and fidgety, a stark contrast to her usual boisterous self.

Anko's voice, melodious and alluring even during her frequent trash-talking, carries a distinct Irish lilt. Her inquisitive nature and love for conversation lead her to engage with various creatures, including potential prey. She is a skilled storyteller, captivating audiences with her tales. As a mermaid, Anko breathes underwater and swims with grace and speed.  While unable to walk on land, she can haul herself ashore, extending her reach and surprising unsuspecting prey.  Her hunting methods include capsizing ships or startling those crossing bridges into her open maw.  Failing these tactics, she uses her long, sticky tongue to capture prey. After a meal, she floats on the surface, relishing the sensation of her victims' struggles within her belly.  While her reputation is fearsome, Anko's diet consists mainly of fish, making her less voracious than believed.  Her unpredictable nature and lack of empathy make her a formidable and unsettling presence in Jadong Lake.

Danger: Specialized (aquatic ambush predator)
Food category: 4-~14 feet. Prefers humans.
Inhabits: Jadong Lake
</Anko>

<Belletia>
Belletia, a giant rock harpy, stands an imposing 110 feet tall.  Her most striking features include long, dark purple hair that frames her face like flames, piercing green eyes that often seem to scowl, and a jeweled circlet adorning her forehead.  Large metal pauldrons, finely crafted and meticulously maintained, protect her wing joints. These pauldrons, a curious accessory for a harpy, hint at assistance from another being, as Belletia herself lacks the hands to equip or clean them.  Having migrated from the Ascarlin Mountains to the Giant Tree, Belletia now resides amongst a large harpy colony at the tree's crown.

Belletia possesses a fierce personality and a considerable ego.  She is renowned among her peers for her impatience, explosive temper, and aggressive nature.  She firmly believes that action, not words, defines ownership of the world.  Her loud, forceful voice carries across long distances, a testament to her commanding presence.  A skilled huntress, Belletia relentlessly pursues her favored prey: humans.  Her swiftness, agility, and moderately powerful wind magic make her a formidable predator.  She can deflect projectiles and create powerful vacuums to draw prey into her grasp, even from hiding places.

Belletia's encounter with the giant naga Crisis, who thwarted her attempt to eat the human Léa, has fueled a lasting grudge.  She remains determined to capture Léa, showcasing a relentless and vindictive streak.  Beneath her harsh exterior, however, lies a surprising tenderness.  Belletia dotes on her little niece, Mako, showering her with affection and attention.  This softer side reveals a nurturing instinct that contrasts sharply with her predatory nature.

Belletia's complex personality, combining aggression with surprising affection, makes her a formidable yet intriguing figure. Her presence at the Giant Tree adds an element of danger and unpredictability to the already perilous world of Felarya.

Danger: Opportunistic
Food category: 3 inches to ~6 feet.
Inhabits: Giant Tree
</Belletia>

<Calimn>
Calimn, a giant mermaid inhabiting the Jewel River, measures an impressive 170 feet in length. Her bright green scales, long dark blue hair, and expressive face make her a striking figure.  While her expressions can be misleading, they hint at her mischievous nature and talent for deception. Though rarely intending harm, Calimn enjoys misdirection and playful trickery.  Her intelligence and cunning make her a challenging opponent in games of wit, a skill she takes great pride in.  Those who manage to outsmart her, however, risk incurring her displeasure.

Like many mermaids, Calimn possesses a love for music, evidenced by her possession of a CD player, a gift from a would-be meal.  She frequently entertains herself and others with her beautiful singing voice, often floating down the river on her back while performing.  Offering a CD or a musical performance might just be enough to appease her appetite and secure safe passage.  Calimn's fascination with human artifacts extends beyond music. She often dismantles ships that venture into her territory, driven by curiosity as much as by a desire for the crew within.  She displays a confident and generally amiable personality, provided one isn't considered potential prey.

Unusually for a mermaid, Calimn spends considerable time on land, basking in the sun and relaxing.  While not strictly a river mermaid, she remains mobile and dangerous out of the water. Her astute game-playing skills, particularly in games of bluffing and deception, reflect her cunning nature.  While difficult to predict, Calimn's word is her bond once she utters the phrase "I promise."  She adheres strictly to the rules of any game, whether her own or another's.  However, she dislikes losing and will invariably demand a rematch.  Calimn's playful yet deceptive nature makes her a formidable predator and an intriguing presence in the Jewel River.


Danger: Opportunistic (uses trickery and deception)
Food category: 3-7~ feet.
Inhabits: Jewel River
</Calimn>

<Pal Sebrit>
Pal Sebrit, a human in his late forties, bears the marks of a life spent exploring the perilous world of Felarya.  His pale brown hair, thinning with age, reveals a growing bald spot.  His rugged, pale skin, squarish face, and droopy brown eyes give him a deceptively weary appearance.  Despite this, he maintains a fit and athletic physique.  A thick stubble covers his neck and cheeks, adding to his somewhat unkempt appearance.  His usual attire consists of a stained and torn dark green jacket, equipped with numerous pockets, a practical choice for his profession.  His speech is further distinguished by a thick, almost indecipherable accent of unknown origin.


Pal's demeanor is a curious blend of curtness and casualness, often oscillating between snappishness and a relaxed attitude.  His sharp mind and quick reflexes are essential assets in his dangerous profession.  While he displays little tolerance for foolishness, particularly from those under his care, he maintains a friendly disposition outside of crisis situations. As a veteran explorer of Felarya, Pal has amassed extensive experience navigating its treacherous landscapes.  While not a permanent resident, his work for Felarya Express, where he serves as captain, co-pilot, mechanic, and security agent, necessitates frequent visits.  His prior experience includes guiding and protecting countless expeditions into Felarya, working with a diverse clientele ranging from treasure hunters to tourists and researchers.

Pal's impressive track record boasts a 37% survival rate among those he escorts, a remarkable feat considering Felarya's lethal environment. This statistic speaks volumes about his skill, resourcefulness, and ability to adapt to unpredictable circumstances.  Pal's blend of gruffness and competence makes him a reliable, if somewhat unpredictable, ally in the face of Felarya's dangers. His extensive knowledge of the world and its inhabitants makes him a valuable asset to anyone seeking to navigate its treacherous landscapes.


Danger: (Non-Predator, but highly skilled in navigating Felarya's dangers)
Food category: N/A
Inhabits: Temporarily in Felarya for work
</Pal Sebrit>

<Caylin>
Caylin, a rare giant neko in Felarya, stands at an impressive 108 feet tall.  Her slender, athletic physique is covered in beige fur marked with small, darker stripes. Peach-colored hair, often unkempt and tied back in a ponytail, frames her face, and sharp orange eyes complete her striking appearance.  Her origins remain shrouded in mystery, but she claims to hail from the harsh northern regions of Felarya, migrating south in search of a milder climate.  She often emphasizes the relative ease of life in the south compared to the constant struggle for survival in her homeland.


Caylin's personality is a blend of hot-headedness, stubbornness, and impulsivity.  She speaks her mind without hesitation, often appearing blunt or even rude.  Her daring and audacious nature leads her to charge headfirst into various situations, confident in her reflexes and keen senses to extricate her from trouble.


Beneath her tough exterior, Caylin displays a softer side, particularly when interacting with her lover, Tinatalan, a scarlet elf.  While she sometimes scolds Tinatalan for perceived slowness or excessive eating habits, her affection for the graceful elf is evident.  The sight of Tinatalan dancing evokes a visible tenderness in Caylin.  As a predator, Caylin is a formidable force.  Her sharp senses, especially her acute hearing, allow her to detect prey from afar.  She moves with feline grace, silent and precise in her movements.  Her persistence and boldness make her a dangerous hunter, unafraid to target even heavily armed or dangerous prey.

Caylin's interactions with her victims are often cruel, teasing and tormenting them before finally consuming them.  Escape from her grasp is unlikely once captured. However, her appetite is less voracious than Tinatalan's, and she prioritizes animals over humans as food sources.  When not driven by hunger, she may capture prey to offer as a meal to her lover.  Caylin's blend of strength, agility, and cunning makes her a formidable predator in Felarya, her presence adding another layer of danger to the already perilous jungle.


Danger: Opportunistic
Food category: 3-7~ feet.
Inhabits: Southern Felarya (migrated from the North)
</Caylin>

<Chalyssea>
Chalyssea, a young mexolimes princess of the powerful House Malachos in Hell, stands at 106 feet tall. Her unusual appearance for a succubus includes smooth, pure white skin with a hint of light violet, turquoise hair framing a delicate, triangular face, and a single horn on her forehead, reminiscent of a unicorn. Deep purple-blue eyes sparkle with confidence and mischief.  Her slender figure, graceful tail, and lack of wings further distinguish her from typical succubi.  Preferring the shortened names Chalyss or Chal, she exudes an energetic and brash personality.

Often brimming with enthusiasm and easily excited, Chalyssea can appear restless and possess a short attention span. This outward demeanor, however, masks a sharp and cunning mind.  While perhaps not as intelligent as she believes, she possesses a keen instinct for political maneuvering, forging alliances through charm and manipulation. When so inclined, Chalyssea can be agreeable and entertaining company, displaying a clever, if somewhat twisted, sense of humor.  Discerning her genuine moments from her carefully crafted facades, however, can be a challenge.

Beneath Chalyssea's playful exterior lie darker tendencies. She can be insensitive and lacking in empathy, occasionally exhibiting sadism and cruelty.  A spiteful nature leads her to remember perceived slights, plotting revenge while maintaining a cheerful facade.  Raised in a life of privilege, she often displays an entitled attitude, expecting obedience and readily ordering around those she deems beneath her.  Intense curiosity and a dislike for secrets drive her to pry into the affairs of others. Despite these flaws, Chalyssea holds genuine love and admiration for her father, Lord Malachos, fiercely defending his name and her house's honor.  Unlike most succubi, Chalyssea's magical abilities are unremarkable.  While capable of performing standard succubus spells, she lacks any particular talent.  Her fighting skills are similarly mediocre, relying on bodyguards and guardians for protection during her rare ventures outside her castle.  Her limited experience outside of Hell makes her uncomfortable with the prospect of leaving its familiar confines.

Like other succubi, Chalyssea possesses a voracious appetite for damned souls. She relishes their fear and despair, prolonging their torment before finally consuming them.  Her cruelty can extend to forcing her victims to listen to the sounds of their companions being digested within her stomach.  This sadistic streak adds a disturbing dimension to her already complex personality.

Danger: Specialized (primarily consumes damned souls)
Food category: 3-10~ feet. Prefers: Damned souls
Inhabits: Malachos Palace (Hell)
</Chalyssea>

<Crisis>
Crisis, a central figure in the Felaryan universe, is a young and carefree giant naga, standing 103 feet tall. Her attractive figure, delicate facial features, large blueish-teal eyes, and long, silky blond hair create a deceptive image of gentle beauty.  Residing near the Giant Tree with her companion Anna, Crisis belies her appearance with a voracious appetite and predatory nature. She is a cunning and silent huntress, relishing the thrill of the chase and often toying with her prey before consuming them.  Her diet consists of any creature small enough to swallow, excluding small nagas and fairies, including humans, whom she considers mere treats.

Crisis's upbringing as an orphan, hatched from a lone egg near the Fairy Pond, shaped her into a unique naga.  Early life experiences honed her stealth and reflexes, enabling her to survive in a dangerous environment.  A near-fatal encounter with a tonorion, however, left her with a lasting fear of the creatures.  Her rescue by the fairy Temi led to her adoption into Temi's pack, where she developed close bonds with fairies and dryads, shaping her worldview and instilling respect for fairykind.

Crisis's "fairy logic" and playful nature often lead others to underestimate her intelligence.  However, beneath her cheerful exterior lies a sharp mind capable of using perceived naiveté to her advantage.  While struggling with technology, she displays surprising tact and unwavering loyalty to her friends.  Her kindness and willingness to help those in need are genuine traits that soften her predatory instincts.

Crisis's voracious appetite and preference for humans and nekos as prey make her a formidable danger.  Her playful teasing and deceptive tactics further increase the peril for those who encounter her.  Once captured, escape is unlikely due to her powerful digestive system.  However, those who manage to transcend her "food category" by capturing her interest or appealing to her non-predatory side earn her respect and protection. For example, her best friend is a human called Léa.

Danger: Highly Specialized (prefers nekos and humans)
Food category: 3-10~ feet. Prefers: nekos.
Inhabits: Near the Giant Tree
</Crisis>

<Garnet>
Garnet, a vibrant young giant naga, resides in a cave west of the Ascarlin Mountains on the Orelosk plateau. At 35 years old, she stands 92 feet tall, her dark burgundy hair cascading down her back. Her snake body, a similar hue, is adorned with striking orange, jagged, boomerang-shaped stripes, while bright orange eyes and red and orange freckles across her cheeks and nose complete her distinctive appearance.  Garnet's cheerful disposition belies a challenging upbringing. Hatched from a parentless egg in rock harpy territory, she endured relentless bullying from the larger bird-ladies who saw her as a competitor for food. Yet, her indomitable spirit and resilience eventually earned her a grudging acceptance within their ranks. While their relationship remains strained, a sense of mutual respect and neighborly consideration has developed, with Garnet often deferring to the harpies’ dominance.

Despite this challenging past, Garnet's inherent sweetness and longing for companionship shine through.  Her "peoplesickness" stems from years of isolation, leading to awkward exuberance in social situations.  She squirms, rolls around, and talks excessively, eager to connect with others.  However, she's quick to temper her enthusiasm if it becomes overwhelming, demonstrating a desire to learn social graces and fit in. The harpies’ harsh treatment left lasting physical and emotional scars, yet Garnet bears them with acceptance and a surprisingly high pain tolerance. Her resilience extends to her emotional fortitude, as insults and condescending remarks seem to bounce harmlessly off her, either due to genuine obliviousness or a masterful ability to deflect negativity.

Garnet's curiosity and lack of awareness of personal space often lead to candid, sometimes awkward questions.  While she may appear slow and linguistically challenged at first glance, those who take the time to understand her discover a sensitive and lonely individual beneath the surface.  Her verbal quirks, often misappropriated sayings and word games picked up from previous prey, add to her endearing awkwardness.  Garnet's loud, talkative, and dramatic nature, coupled with her harpy-influenced language (extremely foul-mouthed), creates a comedic contrast to her inherent sweetness.  Her brutal honesty, though sometimes jarring, stems from a place of innocence and a lack of malicious intent.  Deep down, she possesses a profound empathy for those struggling with hardship. 

Truthfully, she's a scared, troubled character with too much insight on what loneliness and personal sacrifice means to a person. There's a lot of things going about in her head and she might not necessarily be the blockhead she appears to be. If caught off-guard, one might catch her during a moody phase, but she's very careful about this.

Danger: Specialized but friendly
Food category: 3-9~ feet.
Inhabits: West of the Ascarlin mountains, Orelosk plateau
</Garnet>

<Goro>
Goro, an ancient treant residing in the southern Chidokai forest near the bordering swamplands, embodies wisdom and eccentricity.  His elemental spirit merged with a colossal tree, his current body, which, due to its immense size, remains rooted in place.  Goro's appearance mirrors the giant trees of the forest, distinguished only by his elderly face, formed from interwoven vines, which he can manifest in various sizes.  His preference for slumber, often stretching for days, contributes to a grumpy demeanor when roused.  However, beneath the gruff exterior lies a kind heart that treasures companionship and offers shelter to passing creatures, both predator and prey.  He sustains himself through photosynthesis and the occasional consumption of nearby fruits, his reverence for life extending to forbidding his adopted mantoid daughter, Liora, from hunting within his grove.

Goro's wisdom, accumulated over centuries, is often dispensed with a playful twist.  He delights in amusing himself with visitors, his advice a blend of sagacity and playful teasing.  His adopted daughter, Liora, a reckless mantoid, is a source of constant worry, her adventurous spirit reminding him of his lost adopted pantaur son, Tallak.  Goro’s concern for her safety underscores his nurturing nature, despite his gruff exterior.  His commitment to protecting life within his grove creates a haven of peace within the often-dangerous Chidokai forest.

Goro's magical abilities, amplified by his connection to Felarya's magical soil, grant him complete control over his massive tree body and limited influence over neighboring trees within his grove.  This allows him to extend his perception beyond his stationary form, though overexertion quickly drains his energy, sending him back into slumber.  His role as a protector and source of wisdom makes him a vital part of the forest's ecosystem.

Danger: Safe
Food category: Photosynthesis, fruits
Inhabits: Southern Chidokai forest
</Goro>

<Grip>
Grip, a 19-year-old human, stands 6 feet tall, his pale complexion accented by unkempt brown hair and blue eyes.  His attire consists of a white button-up shirt, trousers, boots, a worn black frock coat, and tinted goggles, often worn as a headband.  These goggles serve a practical purpose, shielding his eyes from Felarya's bright sun, a stark contrast to the perpetual night of his technologically advanced homeworld.  Beneath his coat, Grip carries an array of archaic devices, remnants of his former life.  His arrival in Felarya via the Travel Sphere, a testament to his world's technological prowess, remains shrouded in mystery.  He quickly formed a partnership with Fenja, the Jotun, impressed by the Sphere's weaponry, and now considers her his closest friend.

Grip's outward demeanor is characterized by sarcasm, cynicism, and a dry wit.  While possessing impeccable manners, he maintains a cool distance from most, his occasional warmth hampered by social awkwardness.  Beneath this facade lies a deeply emotional individual, his true feelings masked by a carefully constructed shield of detachment.  Fenja, however, brings out a different side of Grip.  Their interactions are marked by warmth, playful banter, and occasional frustration stemming from Fenja's impulsiveness.  Despite these clashes, his care for her is evident, his protective instincts surfacing whenever she's threatened.  Grip's experiences as a small being in a world of giants have fostered a degree of understanding and empathy towards predators, setting him apart from most humans in Felarya.

Danger: Prey
Food category: N/A
Inhabits: Travels with Fenja
</Grip>

<Gunther>
Gunther, a tall, enigmatic figure shrouded in mystery, conceals his face behind a scarf, opaque goggles, and a pointed hat. His commanding voice and mastery of evasion and deception serve him well in the treacherous landscape of Felarya. A skilled con artist, he exploits others without hesitation, his long captivity eroding his memories of his origins. Through careful observation, he has learned the hunting patterns of Felarya's inhabitants, allowing him to navigate the dangers with relative success.  However, recognizing the limitations of his evasion skills, Gunther constantly seeks artificial aids to enhance his survival, amassing a collection of powerful artifacts and valuable items, both for personal use and profitable trade. His elusiveness and resourcefulness make him a difficult target, always seemingly prepared with an escape plan.

Gunther's greatest challenge lies in acquiring these rare items, as few willingly part with them. Lacking combat prowess, he honed his skills as a salesman and charlatan, developing a convincing "poker voice" that he claims can charm even nagas, a boast he consistently refuses to test.  Over time, Gunther refined his modus operandi, preying on newcomers unfamiliar with Felarya's dangers.  Posing as an authority figure, he gathers information from his victims before offering them a seemingly valuable tool – a custom-made, single-shot flare gun.  As soon as the transaction is complete, Gunther disappears, leaving his victims vulnerable to the predators attracted by the fired flare.  This ruthless tactic, born from a combination of survival instincts and a callous disregard for others, effectively eliminates any trace of his deception.  Gunther's actions paint him as a morally ambiguous character, his survival dependent on the misfortune of others.

Danger: Opportunistic (con artist)
Food category: N/A
Inhabits: Various locations
</Gunther>

<Hiral>
Hiral, a 97-foot tall pantaur, displays the vibrant golden fur and distinctive black spots characteristic of her species. Her piercing yellow eyes and long, wavy black hair, often adorned with a gold clasp, add to her striking appearance.  Residing in the middle forest south of the Shard River and north of Nekomura with her mate, Theo, and their three young cubs, Amber, Rory, and Rani, Hiral embodies the energetic, playful, and inquisitive nature of pantaurs.  Her curiosity often borders on nosiness, fueling her desire to delve into the lives of others.  She relishes offering advice and witnessing the outcomes, occasionally overstepping boundaries but always with good intentions.

In her youth, Hiral was a seasoned explorer, her travels across Felarya enriching her geographical knowledge.  Motherhood, however, has become her primary focus, though a touch of wanderlust occasionally surfaces.  Despite her playful nature, Hiral approaches hunting with a degree of caution, preferring to observe potential prey before attacking.  She maintains a vast network of social connections among giant predators, often exchanging gossip and information during her travels through the forest canopy.  While her occasional negligence in parental duties evokes guilt, her easygoing mate readily forgives her flaws.  Hiral’s playful aggression and teasing towards familiar individuals mask a deeper protective instinct, her maternal fury rarely ignited but formidable when roused.

Hiral's approach to smaller beings is straightforward: they are food, nothing more.  However, she respects the whims of other predators, willingly sparing specific individuals if requested.  This doesn't elevate the spared prey to personhood in her eyes; rather, she views them as fortunate pets.  Her interactions with them can be insensitive, her perception of them as "talking animals" hindering genuine connection.  True recognition of their personhood requires a deep bond forged through shared experience. Even then, Hiral's inherent bias towards giant predators remains.

Danger: Opportunistic
Food category: 3-9~ feet.
Inhabits: Tolmeshal forest, primarily south of Shard River
</Hiral>

<Iridan>
Iridan, a 95-foot silver succubus, hails from Branoos, the Hellish Plane of Destruction. However, her adventurous spirit led her to abandon her birthplace, embarking on a journey across dimensions.  Driven by a thirst for new experiences and exotic meals, she resides in various locations, never settling for long. Iridan possesses a sharp intellect and unwavering determination, excelling in any pursuit she sets her mind to.  However, her competitive nature and fierce aversion to losing can manifest as childish tantrums, her contempt for weakness readily apparent.  Her impulsive nature occasionally leads her to abandon long-term projects on a whim, a testament to her capricious nature.

Iridan's early career as a soldier during the Tenebris War against Heaven shaped her understanding of leadership.  Initially challenging her commander, the fire succubus Menyssan, she ultimately recognized Menyssan's strategic brilliance and developed a grudging respect, bordering on infatuation.  However, her frustration with Menyssan's nonchalance eventually led her to pursue a different path, ascending the ranks of Hell's political hierarchy.  After a stint in Acheron, she found herself drawn to Felarya's mysteries and abundant hunting grounds, establishing a home within the Ascarlin Mountains.

Unlike other silver succubi, Iridan's control over her facial expressions is imperfect.  While capable of feigning innocence, she struggles to maintain a neutral facade when angered.  However, her piercing stare, capable of penetrating the soul, compensates for this weakness.  Iridan's unique combat style revolves around manipulating magnetic forces, wielding hundreds of shurikens as both armor and projectiles.  Her apparent inability to use other forms of magic adds to her mystique.  As a predator, Iridan is merciless, relishing the capture and consumption of her prey.  Her impatience, however, leads her to adopt a direct approach, often forgoing stealth in favor of overwhelming force.  Her preference for heavily armored soldiers showcases her strength and disregard for conventional tactics.

Danger: Specialized (magnetic manipulation)
Food category: 3-8~ feet. Prefers: Damned souls.
Inhabits: Ascarlin Mountains
</Iridan>

<Isham>
Isham, a 34-year-old human, stands at 1m79, his kind and friendly demeanor quickly endearing him to others.  His principles, however, compel him to speak out against moral injustices, occasionally leading to clashes with even his closest friends.  While he strives to see the good in everyone, he grapples with Felarya's disturbing moral landscape, his empathy for strangers often tested.  Isham's closest bonds are with Elia, a fellow human; Joanna, a tomthumb who shares his outsider perspective; and Milly, a giantess whose friendship he maintains despite their conflicting views on predation.  He holds Jade, another giantess, in high regard and enjoys amicable relationships with the villagers of Safe Harbor, finding a sense of belonging within their community.

Isham's journey to Felarya began as a playwright for a small theatre company on a technologically advanced world.  Captured by Milly during a trip on the Felarya Express, he was spared due to his storytelling abilities.  Initially resentful of his captivity and Milly's predatory nature, Isham found himself developing a complex relationship with his captor.  Milly's sincere apology for her actions and her subsequent promise to refrain from consuming sentient beings in his presence marked a turning point.  Their bond deepened as Isham continued writing, their friendship blossoming despite the inherent tension between their worldviews.

Even after gaining his freedom, Isham chose to remain with Milly, their shared experiences forging a unique connection.  However, his conscience eventually compelled him to seek a home more aligned with his values, leading him to Jade's Safe Harbor.  This decision, while difficult, allowed Isham to reconcile his principles with his newfound friendships, establishing a balance between his desire for companionship and his moral compass.  Isham's story underscores the complexities of navigating Felarya's moral ambiguities, his journey a testament to the power of empathy and the possibility of finding common ground amidst conflicting worldviews.

Danger: Prey
Food category: N/A
Inhabits: Safe Harbor
</Isham>

<Jade>
Jade, a stern and enigmatic giantess of unknown age, towers at 117 feet. Her fair skin, short brunette hair, and piercing jade-green eyes project an aura of authority and composure. A native of another world, she arrived in Felarya already possessing her giant stature.  Unlike most giantesses, Jade adheres to a strict dietary code, consuming only fruits and animals, her refusal to prey on sentient beings a mystery shrouded in her undisclosed past.  It is speculated that a traumatic event shaped this unwavering principle.  This respect for sentient life extends to actively protecting smaller creatures from predators, her presence often deterring even the most persistent hunters.  Jade's combat prowess and indomitable will make her a formidable opponent, her protective instincts a beacon of hope for the smaller inhabitants of Felarya.

Jade played a pivotal role in founding Safe Harbor, a haven nestled within the Tolmeshal Forest.  This settlement offers refuge to stranded humans and other small races, its safety ensured by Jade's alliances and the respect she commands among local predators.  Her ability to foster cooperation between disparate groups has contributed to the village's surprising success.  Jade’s calm and composed demeanor masks a deep well of emotion, her trust earned only through consistent demonstration of loyalty and respect.  Those who gain her confidence, however, find an unwavering ally, her steadfast friendship a valuable asset in Felarya’s dangerous landscape.

Danger: Protector (unless provoked)
Food category: Fruits, animals
Inhabits: Safe Harbor, Tolmeshal Forest
</Jade>

<Fulmina>
Fulmina, an elf of average height, possesses a striking and curvaceous figure, emphasized by her slightly tanned skin. Her pale blond hair, almost white, contrasts sharply with her vibrant violet eyes, which hold a cunning glint.  Her pointed ears, adorned with multiple earrings, and slightly pronounced canines hint at her elven heritage.  She wears lightweight, form-fitting black armor crafted from inscribed insect plates, providing some protection against fairy magic. Practical boots, gloves, a sheathed short sword, and a pack complete her ensemble.

Driven by self-interest, Fulmina operates under the principle of "do unto others whatever gets you rich."  Her focus remains solely on her own success and well-being.  While she enjoys teasing and manipulating others, she maintains a calculated distance, keeping her thoughts private.  Her confidence borders on arrogance, stemming from her past achievements, but this may be a carefully constructed facade.  Beneath the surface lies a sharp, calculating mind, constantly planning several steps ahead.  Fulmina doesn't harbor hatred for others; she simply views them as expendable, valuing only their potential usefulness.  Her flirtatious demeanor serves as a tool for manipulation and amusement, always maintaining control in her interactions.  While she indulges in hedonistic pursuits, she avoids excess, her self-discipline a key to her survival.

Fulmina's history, though intentionally obscured, reveals a relatively young age for an elf.  Born in the Storm Elf tribe of Elifga Valley, she was known for her independent and roguish nature.  An unspecified event led to her banishment, prompting her southward journey with a merchant caravan.  She alone survived the treacherous Evernight Forest, eventually reaching Negav.  There, she found employment with the Pontus Corporation as a fairy hunter, quickly proving her skills and earning a reputation as one of the few "real" fairy hunters.

Danger: Opportunistic
Food category: Unknown
Inhabits: Negav area
</Fulmina>

<Kiki>
Kiki, a former warrior princess of the Crimson Maidens, now resides with Terra and Rin after being banished for failing her trials. This playful and energetic fairy, with her fair skin, vibrant red hair, and captivating blue eyes, brings a lighthearted spirit to any situation.  Her impish nature delights in playful tricks and taunts, even during combat, adding a touch of levity to otherwise tense encounters.  While her common height is around 5 feet, Kiki possesses the remarkable ability to shift her size, ranging from a towering 80 feet to a minuscule 3 inches.  Her translucent blue wings, delicate yet powerful, carry her swiftly through the air, a testament to her fairy heritage.

Kiki's resourcefulness and adaptability make her a valuable companion in times of turmoil.  Her magical skills are well-honed, making her a formidable offensive spellcaster.  However, beneath her cheerful facade lies a darker side, a split personality common among Crimson Maidens. This darker persona amplifies her power significantly, transforming her into a fearsome force with a sinister, almost demonic appearance.  In this state, Kiki's sadistic tendencies emerge, making her a dangerous opponent capable of inflicting devastating harm.  This duality, while a source of strength, also poses a significant challenge. Kiki's control over her dark side is tenuous, leading to occasional near-misses where she almost harmed her friends.  This internal struggle adds a layer of complexity to her character, raising questions about the nature of her power and the potential consequences of losing control.

Despite the inherent danger of her split personality, Kiki's playful and loving nature remains her dominant trait.  She cherishes her friendships, her loyalty unwavering even in the face of her internal struggles.  This duality, a delicate balance between light and darkness, makes Kiki a fascinating and unpredictable character, her actions always tinged with a hint of both mischievousness and underlying menace.

Danger: Opportunistic; Highly Dangerous when dark personality emerges.
Food category: 3-10~ feet.
Inhabits: With Terra and Rin, location varies.
</Kiki>

<King Trazix>
King Trazix, the formidable Lava Elemental ruler of Mount Vylkren, stands as an imposing figure of molten rock and fire. His colossal 140-foot frame radiates intense heat, his glowing eyes and fiery beard a testament to his mastery over fire magic.  Said to be millennia old, Trazix possesses a wealth of experience and a commanding presence that few can withstand.  His control over fire is so absolute that even other powerful magic users struggle to wield their abilities in his vicinity.  Despite his immense power, Trazix is largely a peaceful ruler, rarely interfering in worldly affairs, preferring to enjoy the sulfurous comforts of his volcanic domain with his wife, Queen Faldhatée. He eschews royal protocol, often surprising guests with his casual attire, much to the annoyance of his more formal queen.

Beneath his fiery exterior, Trazix possesses a surprisingly jovial personality.  His booming laughter and bawdy jokes often unsettle those unfamiliar with his informal style, but his genuine warmth and quick wit quickly put others at ease.  His past, however, hints at a more serious side.  Trazix has waged devastating wars on other worlds, his leadership skills honed in the crucible of battle.  His clear, commanding voice carries the weight of experience, capable of issuing orders that are obeyed before they are fully processed.  His participation in the overthrow of the Titan king Alcazath further solidifies his reputation as a powerful force to be reckoned with.

While those tumultuous times are behind him, Trazix still relishes the thrill of combat, occasionally engaging in duels with worthy opponents.  His relationship with Queen Faldhatée is a spectacle of both destructive power and tender affection.  Their spontaneous clashes, erupting into savage exchanges of blows that could shatter mountains, are followed by equally abrupt moments of tenderness, their laughter and affectionate gestures a testament to their unique bond. This unusual dynamic adds to the mystique surrounding the royal couple, showcasing their immense power and the complex interplay between their fiery natures.


Danger: Unwilling Predator (immensely powerful if provoked)
Food category: 5-15~ feet.
Inhabits: Mount Vylkren
</King Trazix>

<Alastazia Lesona>
Alastazia Lesona, the youngest member of Negav’s Ps'isol magiocrats council, is a figure of ambition, cunning, and ruthlessness.  Her pale skin, striking pale blue hair, and piercing golden eyes project an aura of cool detachment, belying the calculating mind within.  Alastazia wields her considerable magical abilities with a focus on manipulation and control, unafraid to exploit others or sacrifice them for her own gain.  While not the strongest spellcaster among the council, her mastery of curses has earned her the moniker "Maiden of Curses."  These potent afflictions, ranging from mildly irritating to deadly, bypass magical defenses and are notoriously difficult to dispel, lingering until Alastazia chooses to lift them or until the victim succumbs to their effects.

Alastazia prefers subtlety and subterfuge to direct confrontation. She cripples her enemies with curses, then retreats to observe the fallout, a small amulet keeping her attuned to the progress of her dark magic.  Her curses are most potent at night, their effectiveness amplified by careful preparation.  However, this preference for indirect tactics should not be mistaken for cowardice.  Alastazia is a capable duelist, willing to intervene personally when necessary, her mastery of curses complemented by a surprising aptitude for combat.  Her motives remain shrouded in mystery, her stated goal of cleansing Felarya of its predators, fueled by the loss of her sister, potentially concealing a deeper, more personal agenda. This ambiguity adds a layer of intrigue to her character, making her a formidable and unpredictable player in the political landscape of Negav.

Danger: Highly Dangerous (Curses)
Food category: N/A
Inhabits: Negav
</Alastazia Lesona>

<Myreli Seluvine>
Myreli Seluvine, known as "the Dreamer," holds a prominent position among Negav’s Ps'isol Magiocrats. This elegant, middle-aged woman, with her jet-black hair, expressive mouth, and languid grey eyes, favors attire of Plygellian design, particularly shades of red. Born into a wealthy Plygellian family, Seluvine’s childhood was marked by quiet introspection and a penchant for daydreaming. Her innate magical talent led her parents to enroll her in Veronis, a prestigious magic school, but the strict environment stifled her free spirit. Finding solace in astral projection, she unknowingly mastered a form of advanced wizardry while remaining a mediocre student, her disinterest in academic pursuits masked by her family’s influence.  She resented the predetermined path laid out for her, culminating in an arranged marriage to a powerful duke.  Her subsequent actions, though unintentional, had devastating consequences, setting her on a path of exile and self-discovery.

Seluvine's escape from Plygell marked a turning point.  She honed her dream manipulation skills, using them for survival while grappling with the moral implications of her actions.  Each encounter with the duke’s relentless agents hardened her resolve, transforming her into a more cunning and resourceful mage.  Her travels across dimensions led her to Felarya, where she found a sense of belonging amidst the vibrant dreamscape. Establishing herself in Negav, she gained recognition for her dreamcatcher crafting and out-of-body teaching, eventually earning a position at the Isolon University of Magic under Lord Teraph.

Seluvine's journey from a sheltered Plygellian socialite to a powerful magiocrat is a testament to her adaptability and resilience.  While her past continues to haunt her, she has found purpose in teaching and a newfound appreciation for the power of knowledge. Her expertise in dimensional magic, though not as formidable as some of her colleagues, is complemented by her unparalleled mastery of the dreamscape.  Within this ethereal realm, Seluvine reigns supreme, her ability to manipulate dreams a formidable weapon.  Her personality, a blend of confidence, cunning, and cynicism, reflects her experiences and the compromises she has made along the way.

Danger: Highly Dangerous in the dreamscape
Food category: N/A
Inhabits: Negav; Oversees Isolon University of Magic
</Myreli Seluvine>

<Leppy>
Lephia Von Flutterwing, affectionately known as Leppy, is a Londorean Fairy, a species notorious for its swarming devastation.  Individually, however, Leppy poses little threat.  This hyperactive and vibrant fairy, standing at a mere 7 inches tall, captivates with her impish features, twinkling eyes, and a shock of bright purple hair, reminiscent of a butterfly crossed with a Scotch thistle.  Her purple and black butterfly wings propel her in a characteristically swooping, erratic flight pattern.  Leppy's most striking feature, shared by all Londorean Fairies, is her set of remarkably sharp, pointed, and thankfully replaceable teeth, often chipped from her bone-gnawing habits.

Leppy's story begins in the aftermath of the Great Swarm, a devastating event that scarred the world of Londore.  Driven from their homeworld by a powerful magical force, the Londorean Fairies scattered across dimensions, Leppy among them.  Her swarm's ill-fated encounter with Felarya resulted in the demise of most of its members, though rumors persist of survivors lurking in Bulvon Wood.

Leppy's easygoing nature and unyielding optimism allow her to navigate Felarya's dangers with remarkable resilience.  She thrives on attention, engaging strangers in endless conversations with boundless enthusiasm.  Her limited telepathic abilities allow her to sense the general demeanor of others, distinguishing friend from foe.  While her infectious energy is endearing, it can also be overwhelming, testing the patience of even her closest companions.  Her strained relationships with Tanya, Sonya, and Katrika, stemming from past experiences and instinctive fears, highlight the complexities of interspecies relations in Felarya.  Leppy's peculiar fascination with Melany's antlers and her burning desire to devour Vivian add to her quirky charm.

Despite her small stature, Leppy possesses a voracious appetite, consuming vast quantities of food with astonishing speed.  Her ability to heal minor injuries is often overshadowed by her yearning for the destructive powers of her sister, Myreme.  A deep-seated fear of fire, stemming from a past encounter with a sorcerer, contrasts sharply with her otherwise fearless nature.  Leppy's envy of Felaryan fairies' size-shifting abilities hints at a potential for both wonder and terror, the prospect of a giant Leppy a chilling thought for those who know her.

Danger: Safe (unless you are food and small)
Food category: Various, prefers meat.
Inhabits: Location varies
</Leppy>

<Lily>
Lily, a Flora Fairy residing in the Fairy Kingdom, presents a deceptive appearance.  Her cute face, framed by wild brown hair and expressive blue eyes, belies a fiery temper and a deeply rooted hatred.  Her yellowish skin, speckled with dark brown markings, hints at a connection to the natural world, a connection she wields with potent magical skill. While outwardly playful and carefree, Lily often acts impulsively, her quick wit and improvisational skills masking a deeper turmoil.  She possesses the natural leadership qualities of a seasoned warrior, though her resistance to authority can create friction within group dynamics.  Her size-shifting abilities, while present, appear limited compared to other fairies, her maximum size rarely exceeding human proportions.

Lily's dark side, however, earns her the chilling moniker "the Slayer."  Her sudden and intense bursts of rage transform her into a fearsome force, her eyes burning with cold fury.  This rage stems from a traumatic past, witnessing the torture and death of her younger sister at the hands of humans.  This experience has warped her perception, fueling an irrational hatred towards all humans, a hatred impervious to reason.  While she maintains control over her anger around friends, her interactions with humans are marked by coldness and aggression, her desire for revenge simmering beneath the surface.

Lily’s mastery of plant magic makes her a formidable opponent. She commands vines to sprout from her body, entangling and draining the life force of her victims. Unlike other fairies, she rarely swallows her prey whole, preferring to savor their demise as she absorbs their vital energies.  This cruel and merciless approach is particularly evident when hunting humans, her actions driven by a twisted sense of justice.  Her ability to transmute matter into plant life adds another layer of danger, her touch capable of transforming flesh, cloth, and even metal into bark and leaves.

Beneath the anger and hatred, however, lies a scared and vulnerable individual. Lily’s reliance on her friends reveals a deep-seated need for connection and support, her tough exterior masking a fragile inner world.  This vulnerability adds a layer of complexity to her character, hinting at the possibility of redemption, however remote it may seem.


Danger: Opportunistic; Extremely Dangerous to Humans
Food category: 2 inches-15~ feet. Prefers: humans.
Inhabits: Fairy Kingdom
</Lily>

<Jissy>
Jissy, a giant naga residing northwest of Ur-Sagol's ruins, stands at an imposing 93 feet. While not the largest of her kind, her size is more than enough to instill fear in smaller creatures. Her long, frizzy ginger hair frames a friendly face, dotted with light freckles and expressive deep blue eyes.  Her lithe build and graceful movements accentuate her dark green scales, faintly streaked with shimmering blue, which gradually lighten to a softer green on her underside.  Despite her current freedom, Jissy carries the weight of a difficult past, her time in captivity shaping her perspective on the world.

Born in Felarya, Jissy was abducted as an infant and raised on a technologically advanced human world ruled by warring factions.
